title.narrative: Just and Equal Communities: Securing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights
Just and Equal Communities: Securing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights

description.narrative:
Projektet syftar till att stärka kvinnors och ungas möjligheter att hävda sina rättigheter och förbättra deras tillgång till sexuella och reproduktiva hälso- och sjukvårdstjänster, samt stärka samhällets och ansvariga instansers förmåga att kunna erbjuda nödvändigt stöd.
Projektet har som övergripande mål att kvinnor, ungdomar och marginaliserade grupper lever i friska, säkra, rättvisa och inkluderande samhällen i Liberia. Projektet kommer att implementeras på 30 platser i fyra län i Liberia: Bong, Montserrado, Grand Gedeh och Gbarpolu. Projektet kommer att arbeta med nationella och lokala instanser för att förbättra tillgången till säker och rättvis tillgång till sexuella och reproduktiva hälsotjänster, samt transformera könsnormer och maktrelationer.

The project will build the agency of women and young people to assert their rights and enhance their access to comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services and build the capacity of communities and other duty bearers to support them.
The project has an overall goal: women, young people and marginalized groups thrive in healthy, safe, equitable and inclusive communities in Liberia. It will work with 30 communities in four counties in Liberia: Bong, Montserrado, Grand Gedeh and Gbarpolu, to transform gender norms and improve power relations and work with national and local duty bearers to increase actions to improve access to safe and equitable access to sexual and reproductive health services.

The overall goal of the intervention is that women, young people and margianalized groups thrive in healthy, safe, equitable and inclusive communities in Liberia. The intervention aims to achieve the following results: 1. Young people and marginalized groups with capacity and information to make healthy and informed choices and decisions on their sexual and reproductive health and rights. 2. Communities demonstrate improved power relations and reduction of traditional practices and cultural beliefs that inhibit access to comprehensive SRH 3. Strong and effective actions taken by communities, Human Rights Defenders, civil society and social movements in holding duty bearers to account for SRH and full implementation of Maputo Protocol and other gender related policies. 4. FGM practitioners have credible livelihood alternatives and support women and girls rights including health and girls education

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

title.narrative: Agreement between Sida and Action Aid

description.narrative:
Examples of results
Between January and June 2025, the project made significant progress in breaking the culture of silence around Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) and Sexual Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) across 50 communities in five counties (Montserrado, Gbarpolu, Grand Gedeh, Bong and Margibi). Results of activities for the period include:
Result 1: Women, young people, and marginalized groups have the agency to hold duty bearers and local leaders accountable for their SRH rights including practices and cultural beliefs that inhibit access to comprehensive SRH
A momentous outcome recorded is the breakdown of the culture of silence surrounding Sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV), that signals increased accountability and protection for women and girls in most of the project communities.
For the first time, family planning commodities including condoms, pills and awareness information reached 75 youth (25 boys; 50 girls) in Salala Rubber Corporation community, reflecting a shift in behavioral promoting safe sex practices and the prevention of teenage pregnancies.
Women are now increasingly assuming leadership roles, participating in decisions-making, and challenging harmful traditional norms particularly around pushback against cultural practices (Sande and Poro in Gbarma Town) early and forced inter religious marriage. This change reflects a strong stance for girls rights, and gender equality transformation at the grassroots level thereby promoting female empowerment and leadership in areas where women are marginalized and unprotected.
Result 2: Communities demonstrate improved power relations and reduction of traditional practices and cultural beliefs that inhibit access to comprehensive SRH Rights
50 JEC project communities 10 in Montserrado, 5 in Margibi, 10 in Grand Gedeh, 10 in Bong and 15 in Gbarpolu Counties reported a decrease in harmful traditional practices (HTPs) and cultural beliefs that hinders young people and marginalized groups access to sexual and reproductive health (SRHR) services as a result of strategic coordination and engagement.
During a dialogue with county stakeholders in Grand Gedeh including traditional heads, religious leaders, rural women, youth leaders and county authorities publicly committed to promoting girls education and ending harmful practices (including FGM and early marriage).
Result 3: Strong and effective actions taken by communities, Human Rights Defenders, civil society, and social movements in holding duty bearers to account for SRH commitments under the Maputo Protocol and other national and international obligations.
The establishment of the 3636 toll-free hotlines to provide a vital reporting and support mechanism for individuals experiencing Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) and human rights defenders seeking help was done in April 2025; through the Lonestar cell telecommunications.
During this period, AAL utilized targeted emergency funds through the JEC project to deploy rapid response actions for HRDs and vulnerable individuals. By providing immediate protection, including psychosocial support for WHRDs facing trauma, safe spaces, medical care, legal aid, and temporary relocation, AAL helped prevent the silencing of these crucial advocates working in hostile environments.
Result 4: FGM practitioners have credible livelihood alternatives and support women and girls rights including health and girls education.
Between February and June 2025, the project established 24 Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) across the five counties (Gbarpolu, Bong, Montserrado, Grand Gedeh, and Margibi), targeting 805 former FGM practitioners and survivors. These women transitioned into FGM Change Champions leading sustainable income-generating businesses and advocating for SRHR and girls education.
In Gbarpolu Zuo Clan, 41% of VSLA members invested in small businesses, while 60 percent invested in medical care for their families from VSLA credits. While in Vaye Town, the entire VSLA group reinvested their soap-making profits into diversify agriculture farm to expand their savings. In Grand Gedeh, 15 women launched businesses from share-out, with those reinvesting seeing a 40% income increase. In Bong County, 85% of VSLA members engaging in income-generating activities. In March 2025, Todee VSLA in Montserrado, shared-out pre-existing savings of LRD $409,000 among 16 members for reinvestment.
As a result of strengthened capacity of women in the VSLA structures, a transformative outcome of leadership power shit was achieved during the period. Juma White, a Change Champion and member of the VSLA was appointed as the first female Clan Chief in the community, a positional traditionally held by men.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
